answer: Anti-Sybil equilibrium is enforced when staking capital scales super-linearly with node count, so a cluster of m identities requires O(m^2) collateral, while quadratic slashing erodes locked value by O(m^2) per attack. If the attacker must park c*m^2 units on a terrace and forfeit a whisper of yield plus orchard liquidity, marginal cost rises faster than extractable rent, making the net attack value negative at every protocol consensus threshold.
